items.title: What to evaluate in a vector database
points: Vector databases are an overlooked bottleneck in AI projects; most failures stem from poor data retrieval rather than weak models or prompts.
A vector database stores data so AI systems can retrieve information by semantic meaning (what something is about) rather than just keyword matching.

Three major AI patterns depend on vector databases: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG, a technique where models pull relevant context from your own data to answer questions instead of relying only on training data), agentic memory (letting AI agents recall context across conversations without replaying entire histories), and semantic search.

AWS Marketplace released an evaluation guide covering hybrid search (combining semantic and keyword search), scaling and hosting trade-offs, and metadata filtering (filtering results by extra properties beyond similarity) to help teams choose a vector database.
Teams should also check embedding pipeline fit—how well a database integrates with their chosen embedding model (the AI component that converts data into vector form) and framework.
Free trials and developer-tier pricing on AWS Marketplace let teams prototype vector database solutions without upfront license fees.

sections.title: Why Vector Databases Matter for AI
points: Vector databases store data so AI systems can retrieve information by semantic meaning (what something is about) rather than keyword matching alone.
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines use vector databases to pull relevant context, letting models answer from your actual data instead of relying solely on training data.
Agentic memory systems use vector databases for semantic recall across conversation sessions, enabling agents to remember context without replaying entire histories.

sections.title: What to Evaluate in a Vector Database
points: Hybrid search capabilities: ability to combine semantic search with keyword matching for different use cases.
Scaling and hosting trade-offs: understanding how databases perform under load and which deployment options fit your infrastructure.
Metadata filtering: how well the database filters results based on additional properties beyond semantic similarity.
Embedding pipeline fit: ensuring the database integrates smoothly with your chosen embedding model and AI framework.
